reasons: The cited Section 15.1–15.2 text contains a genuine Vendor-side (MSL) indemnity running to IBM (our client) covering third-party IP infringement (patent, trademark, copyright, mask work, trade secret), MSL's non-compliance with law, and warranty/support failures, plus standard procedure and procure/redesign remedies — this meets the preferred position's core elements, so 'compliant' is the correct classification.

Exclusions cited (IBM-selected marks, IBM written specifications, IBM-supplied defective designs) are the customary carve-outs contemplated by the fallback and do not defeat the fallback on any material term; no one-way Customer indemnity of Vendor appears, so walk-away territory is not implicated.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was applied (rendered text is identical to the original) and no counterparty comment was drafted; the deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') corroborates this.

Gaps correctly handled as rationale notes rather than deviations: absence of 'and its affiliates', no separate data-breach or gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct trigger, and the 3%-of-bill-of-materials cap which is properly addressed under the limitation-of-liability rule rather than double-flagged here.
